entries.note: This is a loopback-only desktop service. HTTP and WebSocket requests need the private runtime token and compatible Origin; it is not the Quest pairing protocol. Tokens stay in mode-0600 local state, never tracked files. Slow sockets reconnect to bounded retained output without stopping sessions. The retired browser bundle is not served; a later web client needs separate delivery authorization. State advertises handoff and desktopActions version 1. Presented requires a session attached on that socket. Desktop registration/action acknowledgement use the same authenticated events connection; discovery/reload route through the ephemeral desktop broker. These are local workflow bindings, not protection against an authenticated client deliberately forging readiness or displayed roots.

entries.note: The host serves the format registry so a directly connected desktop and the service tests need no supervisor; the replaceable worker serves the same three routes for the live layered runtime whose host predates them. Both advertise formatRegistry: 1. Declared commands run only from format-preview (explicit open/refresh/agent call), never from tree listing. dashboard: 1 and projectGame: 1 tell connectors that the dashboard routes and that game-config answer from the per-project declaration; projectGameLaunch: 1 says the same of the launch, and the host advertises it because it both preflights and spawns. The workspace worker advertises projectGame on its own (it serves game-config from its checkout) but mirrors projectGameLaunch from the host, whose Sessions and Surfaces own the spawn: an older host still launches the removed built-in game, so that half is refused by name rather than forwarded. game-config and game take an optional gameId selecting one declared game; omitted, both use the first declared record, which is what the launcher and an agent calling the tool without arguments get.

The tracker routes are served here and nowhere else, which means a workspace whose session host predates them cannot get them by a layered update: an update replaces the worker, and the host is the one component it cannot replace. That is the KI-043 shape, and it bit the owner — their development workspace, running a host from the previous day, answered 404 for /api/tracker while the desktop binary beside it had the button. The durable fix is the one games took: serve the read from the worker and leave only what genuinely needs the host's own state here. Until that happens, a new route added in this file reaches a running workspace only when its host is replaced.

entries.note: KI-110: this context is the whole binding a pane gets, and until 2026-09-14 it named no runtime directory. Every JS reader survived that because discovery.mjs DEFAULTS the argument -- discoverRuntime(host, directory = runtimeDirectory(host)) -- so resolveRuntime and the mcp.mjs facade computed the same path anyway. red-mcp does not default: workspace.rs returned the session host outright when the field was absent, so every pane was served by the host rather than the root-bound worker and lost the eight capabilities only the worker declares (layeredUpdates, projectWindows, agentToken, scriptActions, ide, agentsMenu, taskWrites, agentSpawn -- measured 12 against 20 on a live launch). The value must be derived from THIS host's own identity, not from a caller's: runtimeDirectory is exactly ensureRuntime's default, so a supervisor bootstrapped from this context lands in the directory the context names, and the document then matches the one runtime/supervisor.mjs:217 writes for a pane of its own. Note the front door mints its own context for panes it starts (red/red-host/src/panes.rs), from ITS identity, which is the instance a live workspace's runtime directory is keyed on; that writer is separate from this one and still omits the field, which is why red-mcp's computed fallback is the half that fixes a running workspace.
